atoms.text: One of the most famous Scottish myths is the Monster of Loch Ness. “Nessie”, as it is called, is believed to live in Loch Ness and has supposedly been sighted several times.
atoms.sound: One of the most famous Scottish myths is the Monster of Loch Ness. Nessie, as it is called, is believed to live in Loch Ness and has supposedly been sighted several times.

text: The plesiosaurus is an extinct reptile that lived in the sea and was up to 20 meters long.

atoms.b: Hey Harris, do you know anything about the myth of the Loch Ness Monster?

Hi Jacky, of course! Nessie, as it is called, was first sighted nearly 1500 years ago and has supposedly eaten a man at the shore. It has a long neck and tail, is about 20 meters long and said to look like a plesiosaurus.
Oh, that sounds thrilling! I think I have seen a picture of it.
Possibly. There are a few famous pictures claiming to show the monster. The first photograph was allegedly taken in the 1930s and since then Nessie is known to look like a dinosaur.
And where can I see it?

Most people believe that Nessie doesn't exist. Nevertheless, hundreds of tourists travel to Loch Ness each year. The lake is near Inverness, a city in the north-east of Scotland. The lake stretches over 36 kilometres and is thereby the longest lake in Scotland. So good luck finding Nessie!

Nessie is a ((++monster fish)) that supposedly lives in ((++Loch_Ness Loch_Inverness)). It was first seen nearly ((++1500 150,000)) years ago. The monster is said to look like a ((++plesiosaurus brachiosaurus)) and to be about ((++20 60)) metres long. The ((++36 19)) kilometre long lake is a tourist hotspot as hundreds come to try and see Nessie each year, although the public opinion is that Nessie does not exist.

atoms.text: The Kelpie is another creature of Scottish folklore. It is a mystic horse with a dripping mane coming from the water.

atoms.b: What about the Kelpie? Do you know anything about it?
I do! The Kelpie is a mystical water horse.
What is that supposed to mean, a water horse?
Legend has it that the Kelpie comes out of the water and seduces people to ride on its back. It would then go back into the water which causes the rider to drown.

It gets even scarier: The Kelpie is said to haunt the lochs and rivers of Scotland. It approaches humans in the form of a lost pony. However, you can identify it by its constantly dripping mane. It is able to take on human form, but it would then still have hooves.
